    Start the GROBID container via Docker

    grobid_docker_start.Rd

    Launches a GROBID container in the background after checking that Docker is installed and operational. If the Docker daemon is not started, an automatic startup attempt is performed. The function then waits for the service to be ready via an HTTP health check.

    Usage

    grobid_docker_start(
  docker_image = .checkrefr_env$docker_image,
  grobid_version = .checkrefr_env$grobid_version,
  model_type = .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type,
  port = .checkrefr_env$docker_port,
  max_ram = "4g",
  pull = FALSE,
  timeout_ready = .checkrefr_env$timeout,
  verbose = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    docker_image

    character(1) Base of the Docker image to use. Default: value of .checkrefr_env$docker_image. Default: "lfoppiano/grobid:"

    grobid_version

    character(1) GROBID version. Default: value of .checkrefr_env$grobid_version. Default: "0.9.0".

    model_type

    character(1) or NULL. GROBID model variant:

    • NULL or "" (default) – no variant specified, the image is used without a suffix ({version}), historical behavior.

    • "full" – image including the Deep Learning and CRF models. Docker tag convention: {version}-full.

    • "crf" – CRF-only image. Docker tag convention: {version}-crf.

    See https://grobid.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Grobid-docker/. Default: .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type.

    port

    integer(1) Local port to expose. Default: 8070.

    max_ram

    character(1) Memory limit for the container. Default: "4g".

    pull

    logical(1) Force downloading of the image. Default: FALSE.

    timeout_ready

    integer(1) Max seconds to wait for GROBID. Default: 120.

    verbose

    logical(1) Display progress messages. Default: TRUE.

    Value

    invisible(TRUE) if the container started and GROBID is responding.

    Details

    The function performs the following steps in order:

    1. Checking that Docker is installed on the system.

    2. Checking that the Docker daemon is running. If not, an automatic startup attempt is performed via .start_docker().

    3. Checking that the requested port is free.

    4. Optional download of the Docker image (pull = TRUE).

    5. Launching the container in the background.

    6. Waiting for the GROBID service to respond (HTTP health check).

    7. Updating the package's internal environment variables.

    See also

    grobid_docker_check() for a simple Docker diagnostic, grobid_remote_connect() to connect to a remote server.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
grobid_docker_start()
grobid_docker_start(grobid_version = "0.8.1", port = 8080)
grobid_docker_start(pull = TRUE, max_ram = "8g")
} # }
